title: Time to edumucate urselves on Litecoin's MWEB with the Unpronounceable Professor.
description:
Special thanks to @flippi-fi for this video!

MWEB stands for MimbleWimble Extension Blocks, a groundbreaking privacy and scalability protocol integrated into the Litecoin blockchain. Named after a tongue-tying spell from the Harry Potter series, MimbleWimble was first proposed in 2016 by an anonymous developer, "Tom Elvis Jedusor," to enhance transaction privacy and blockchain efficiency. Litecoin adopted this technology by a consensus known as miner signaling, activating MWEB on May 19, 2022. MWEB operates as an optional extension of the Litecoin network, running parallel to the main blockchain via extension blocks. It allows users to conduct confidential transactions, hiding the amount of Litecoin (LTC) transferred from public view, while maintaining compatibility with the transparent main blockchain. This makes Litecoin a more private, scalable, and fungible form of digital money.

asr.full_text: Welcome to my Litecoin show i am Prof onkkutwe nkketwe enketwe mbarakwe and today i will be teaching you about private light coins aka mWeb and no i'm not Spider man you will understand in a second mWeb is an extension block attached to every transparent Litecoin block in the blockchain in order to allow for private transactions. This is a transparent Litecoin block in the blockchain in order to allow for private transactions this is a transparent litecoin block running and this is an mweb block running parallel to it they're basically husband and wife you can see the transaction inside the transparent block like your husband that won't shut up but you cannot see any transaction inside the emware block like a wife that never talks so mwa basically protects your Litecoin from the eyes of hackers, stalkers and other bad actors in this space. Now, how do you use private litecoin. Go to a wallet app that has Mweb support like nexus wallet or kick wallet, and allow your litecoins to the mweb. Voilah, you are now private litecoining. Now why do you need private lite coins for that? I will respond with a simple question. Do you post a screenshot of your salary on instagram everytime you receive it? That's it for me today. As usual, I am your Professor. Unkutue, Untuetue, nketue, nbarakwe. And I will see you in the next episode.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents an educational explanation of Litecoin MWEB, using a whiteboard and an analogy about private transactions. It provides practical guidance for moving Litecoin into MWEB through a compatible wallet, but does not present a guaranteed financial return or wealth opportunity. A Nexus Wallet download prompt appears separately, while the available video evidence identifies no payment requirement, credential request, or deceptive outcome.
